learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected They stay at about 1 percent and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Generation zero B share 1.0 percent, average A 1.99 and B 2.01, edge 0.02. Ten generations gave 1.1 percent; twenty 1.2. Run to 120 gave displayed 100 percent and edge 2.00. Restart restored 1 percent and initial edge; rerun reproduced 100 percent.
observations.reveal: Corrected to slowly then fast, described 2 percent by gen 50, 21 by 100 and 99 by 111. Defined all-A Nash equilibrium but not evolutionary stability using B versus B advantage. Toy chosen payoffs and no real-species claim explicit.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Offspring payoff table, slow-then-steep share curve and numeric edge aligned. Reveal text and model caveat legible, with lower card extending to viewport edge.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete payoff table supports a nontrivial spread commitment.
prediction.evidence: Tie against A but advantage in B encounters.

interaction.reason: Early steps versus long run and restart reveal timescale contrast.
interaction.evidence: 1.1 at ten, 1.2 at twenty, 100 displayed at 120.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects accelerating share to frequency-dependent encounters.
payoff.evidence: B-B advantage grows as B becomes common.

clarity.reason: Rows, opponent columns and score meaning are explicit.
clarity.evidence: Surviving offspring and random meetings labels.

transfer.reason: Definitions and conditions are explained within chosen game, no fresh application.
transfer.evidence: Nash equilibrium versus evolutionary stability distinguished.

accessibility.evidence: Payoff table and share summary exposed as text; keyboard, screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Tying residents does not prevent eventual invasion.

visualExplanation.reason: Curve and changing average edge show positive feedback.
visualExplanation.evidence: Flat early share followed by steep rise.

playfulness.reason: Stepping and running a model reveals delayed behavior.

practicalValue.evidence: Toy model explicitly not real species.

depth.reason: Separates unilateral equilibrium from evolutionary invasion under frequency dependence.
depth.evidence: Second-order encounter advantage and no baseline offspring.

complexity.reason: Easy controls introduce payoff matrices and two distinct stability concepts.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Compute opponent-weighted offspring and infer frequency-dependent invasion despite direct tie.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Nash equilibrium and evolutionary stability introduced at reveal.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Two by two payoff table, percentages and average score differences.

whyCool: A mutant can creep almost invisibly until meeting its own kind makes growth accelerate.
caveat: Chosen deterministic payoff model has no baseline offspring and does not establish real-population invasion behavior.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
